extracts.text:
ABSTRACT

Social Welfare and Women Empowerment - “Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme” in the place of Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Memorial Marriage Assistance Scheme — Implementation Guidelines - Orders - Issued.

Social Welfare and Women Empowerment [SW3(2)] Department

G.O. (Ms) No.46 Dated 02.08.2022

SUACHHI Wig. 17 Hlcheuot (om aspiredor (hf 2053

Read:

Letter of Director of Social Welfare, No.5929AWW-1(1)/2022, Dated 06.07.2022.

RKEKKE

During the Budget Speech 2022, the Hon’ble Minister for Finance and Human Resource Management has announced that “recognizing the low enrolment ratio of girl students from Government schools in higher education, the Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Memorial Marriage Assistance Scheme is being transformed as Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme. All girl students who studied from Classes 6” to 12" in Government schools will be paid Rs.1,000/- per month directly into their bank account till the uninterrupted completion of their undergraduate degree, diploma and ITI courses. The students will be eligible for this in addition to other scholarships. Through this programme, approximately 6,00,000 girl students can potentially benefit each year. For this new scheme, an amount of Rs.698.00 crore has been allotted in this Budget. The existing schemes of EVR Maniammaiyar Memorial Widow's Daughter Marriage Assistance Scheme, Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy Memorial Inter-Caste Marriage Assistance Scheme, Annai Teresa Orphan Girls Marriage Assistance Scheme and Dr. Dharmambal Ammaiyar Memorial Widow Remarriage Assistance Scheme will continue to be implemented without any change”.

2. To implement the above announcement, in the letter read above, the Director of Social Welfare has sent proposal based on the various meetings held alongwith implementation modalities of Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme containing the salient features of the Scheme, Design, Mode of Direct Benefit Transfer, Eligibility criteria, Quantum of Amount, Implementation, Convergence, Budget allocation, Administrative cost, Setting up of Programme Management Unit, System Integrator, Roles and responsibilities of State Programme Management Unit/Departments, Banking sector, State/District level Committees, Single Window Service delivery and requested the Government to issue orders in this regard.

3. After careful consideration, Government accept the proposal of Director of Social Welfare and issue the following orders: -

(i) The Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Memorial Marriage Assistance Scheme is transformed as Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme.

(ii) Cash benefit of Rs.1,000/- per month per beneficiary till the completion of their first higher education shall be paid monthly to the girl students who have completed their 6" to 12" std in Government schools of Tamil Nadu and enrolled in any higher education courses in any Higher Education Institutions recognized by Government of Tamil Nadu/ Government of India / University Grants Commission situated in Tamil Nadu.

9. In respect of admission of students under All India category, there is no direction by any lawful authority to the National Law Universities to follow only the Central Scheme of reservation. The Central Scheme of reservation which is otherwise enforced by the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006 (Central Act 5 of 2007) will apply only to certain Central Educational Institutions established, maintained or aided by the Central Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

10. The Tamil Nadu National Law University being a University constituted by the Government of Tamil Nadu under the State enactment and funded by the State Government, there is no legal obligation to follow the Central Scheme of reservation. The surrender of seats to All India category is only an arrangement between the members of Consortium of National Law Universities to become a member of the Said Consortium. There is no instruction or guideline framed by the Consortium with regard to reservation policy to be followed in the admission of National Law Universities.

11. This being the position, it is considered that it is open for the State Government to direct the Tamil Nadu National Law University to follow the State reservation policy in the lines of the reservation mandated by the Tamil Nadu Backward Classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Service under the State) Act, 1993 (Tamil Nadu Act 45 of 1994) for the All India category also and there is no legal impediment to do so. If the Tamil Nadu State’s reservation policy is followed in All India category in the admission of students to Tamil Nadu National Law University, it would be more than the percentage of reservation already given for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in All India category and would very well comply with the directions of National Commission for Backward Classes also.

3.3 FORMATION OF BYPASSES

Bypasses provide an alternate route for the through-traffic in towns and built-up areas to reduce traffic congestion within urban locality and improve the safety of the public. There are two critical phases in construction of bypasses viz., Land Acquisition stage (I- Phase) and formation stage (II- Phase)

In the year 2022-23, 3 bypasses i.e. in Uthiramerur, Tiruppur & Coimbatore Western Ring road have been taken up at a cost of Rs. 435.39 crore. At the beginning of the year, work were going on in 17 nos. of bypasses as spill over. 1 bypass at Iluppur has been completed at a cost of Rs.23 crore and works are at advanced stages in remaining 16 bypasses i.e. Thiruthani, Thiruthurai Poondi- Part-2, Rasipuram (Phase-I Part-2), Conoor,

51

Parthibanoor, Pollachi, Aruppukottai, Bhavani, Ambasamudram, Mudukulathur, Kamuthi, Thiruporur, Tambaram Eastern bypass, Kelambakkam, Sivagangai and Jalakandapuram.

Further, preliminary works on 58 nos of bypasses are at various stages like Land Acquisition, planning and preparation of Detailed Project Report.

3.4 FORMATION OF LINK ROADS

In 2022-23, the Government have accorded administrative sanction for carrying out Link Road at Pasumalai near Thiruparankundram at a cost of Rs. 41.89 crore. The work is in tender Stage. Work on another link road i.e. widening and improving the road connecting Erode - Perundurai - Kangeyam road to Ooty - Kothagiri - Mettupalayam - Sathy - Gobi - Erode road near Kaniravutharkulam via Vilarasampatty, as spill over, at a cost of Rs. 20.85 crore is at advanced stage of completion.

52

3.5 CONSTRUCTION OF HIGH-LEVEL BRIDGES (HLB)

High-Level Bridges are normally constructed to cross over the water bodies along the road alignments. In the last two years, 147 nos of HLBs have been completed and put to public use.

Loan assistance of National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is also availed for construction of High-level River Bridges in lieu of causeways / weak bridges / narrow bridges under Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF). The loan assistance is 80% and balance 20% is met out from State Fund. In the year 2022-23, 158 High Level Bridge (HLB) works have been taken up at a cost of Rs.818.66 crore. In the last two years, 139 Nos of HLBs funded under NABARD assistance at a cost of Rs.382.49 crore have been brought to public use. Works on 136 spill over High Level Bridges at a cost of Rs.888.07 crore are going on.

e Timely action will be taken by the Cell to redress the grievances with the help of the local Police Station having the concerned jurisdictional area.

2.3. HOW TO CONTACT

Complaints / Grievances can be lodged through the newly proposed TN POLICE NRI web portal.

The NRIs can also contact the Superintendent of Police/Deputy Superintendent of Police or Inspectors of Police seeking any legal help with regard to their grievances through their mobile numbers and also through an official whatsapp number / telephone number or through a dedicated e-mail id.

Directions will be given to the concerned Districts / Cities / units to conduct impartial enquiry and FIR will be registered by the local jurisdictional stations if necessary.
